title: IrisScale cold outreach lab + objection playbook
content:
Quick thesis:
- IrisScale Commerce looks like a mid-market omnichannel retail analytics vendor (SaaS + some edge install for POS hooks). Small headcount on infra; likely uses managed infra and cares about latency for live comms and embeddings for search/rerank.

Company snapshot (public + guessed):
- HQ: Denver
- ARR estimate: $7–12M
- Tech: Python backend, Postgres, S3, likely some Redis. Candidate ML workload: product search rerank, chat assistant for merchant support, on-demand embedding index for catalog updates.
- Signal: hiring for "platform" and "ml infra" in last 6 months (GH job posts), mentions real-time search in blog.

Key contacts (who to try):
- Head of Product (LinkedIn: Riley Ortega) — owns roadmap, pilot champion potential
- CTO (LinkedIn: Sanjay Rao) — escalation, security questions
- VP Partnerships / BizDev (LinkedIn: Lena Morales) — procurement + partner pilots

Why Redwood might win here (hypotheses):
- Need for predictable latency + cost for chat/search (can't pay for expensive endpoint bursts).
- They want a single API across hosted/dedicated/private as they have mixed infra (SaaS + hosted on customer sites).
- Eval risk: embeddings accuracy + rerank quality; we can surface Redwood Optimize suggestions and cost/throughput tradeoffs.

Do-not-assume list (open questions to confirm):
- Do they process PHI or regulated PII? (If yes, push private deployment conversation.)
- Are catalogs updated hourly or daily? (drives caching strategy)
- What is peak qps for search? (important for Dedicated vs hosted)

Outbound play (micro-experiments):
A. 6-email cold sequence (short, hypothesis-driven):
  1) Short intro + micro value: "15 min idea: lower search token cost 40% w/ same relevance"
  2) Quick case + ask for 15-min product sync (include a benchmark snapshot)
  3) Tech validation note to CTO (latency/kv-cache angle)
  4) Pilot offer: 3-week, no-surgeon-needed baseline w/ shared eval set
  5) ROI nudge + calendar link
  6) Breakup note + ask for intro

B. SDR + SE jam:
- SDR opens convo with product lead; SE sends short tech note on "how we handle live-catalog embeddings and incremental updates" (one-pager).

Sample top-of-mail subject lines (test):
- "Cut search token spend 30–50% (no model change)"
- "Idea for IrisScale: cheaper, faster catalog search"
- "Quick pilot: 3 weeks to measure search cost/latency tradeoffs"

Objection handling (short riffs):
- "We already have a provider": ask what their unit token cost and token latency look like; offer a side-by-side micro-benchmark on a subset.
- "Security/compliance concerns": If they handle sensitive data, propose Private deployment (VPC + customer KMS). Call out audit logs and SOC/ISO hints.
- "Integration cost": propose a thin shim + SDK (we can map 80% of endpoints in 1–2 days for search/chat). Offer runbook + SE time for pilots.
- "We won’t change model": emphasize we can route their existing model via Redwood and do batching/caching without changing model outputs — savings come from serving optimizations.

Pilot idea (3-week micro-pilot):
- Goal: show cost per query reduction and maintain relevance (NDCG metrics)
- Week 0: dataset selection (10–20k queries, live catalog snapshot), agree success metrics
- Week 1: baseline capture (their current infra), lightweight integration (proxying calls to Redwood).
- Week 2: run Redwood configs — batching + prefix caching + quantized variant, measure latency & cost
- Week 3: compare results, one pager, recommendation + next-step pricing/commit ask

Success metrics to measure (we should propose):
- 95th p95 latency for search rerank (ms)
- tokens per query and tokens-per-catalog-update (unit cost)
- NDCG@10 (relevance) delta vs baseline
- Estimated monthly cost savings at current query volume

Technical talking points for SE to send to CTO/infra:
- Continuous batching with latency SLOs; fallback to lower-cost region/variant on saturation
- KV-prefix caching for repeated product contexts (common for shop pages)
- Quantization/compiled kernels to reduce GPU memory and unit cost
- Option for on-prem/private control plane if compliance demands

CRM notes / next steps (TODOs):
- [ ] Pull LinkedIn emails for Riley, Sanjay, Lena (Ava)
- [ ] Create eval dataset sample (10k queries) — ask product lead for logs
- [ ] Draft SE one-pager on "catalog embedding velocity" (Maya)
- [ ] Run 1 internal micro-benchmark against open model we think they use (Llama-2-13B-ish)
- [ ] Book 30-min discovery if no response after step 2 (Jordan)

Risk checklist (what kills deal quick):
- Heavy regulatory data classification (HIPAA/PCI) without willingness to do private deployment
- Strong incumbent contract (SLA + pricing) with >12 months remaining
- Internal org: no clear product champion

Benchmarks to attach if they ask (we should prepare):
- small table: tokens/query vs tokens/second vs p95 latency — run on model variant X; (we will author once micro-bench runs complete).

Random scratch ideas / experimental angles: (brainstorm, messy)
- Offer a "pilot credits" package where we run side-by-side using their traffic for two weeks and only bill if we hit X% cost savings
- Partner co-marketing: "IrisScale + Redwood: faster search for modern merchants" (if they care about press)
- Run a short webinar targeted to "retail search leads" using IrisScale as a reference (if pilot goes well)

Notes-to-self: short, unpolished
- Keep outreach < 3 paragraphs. Mention specific metric "token spend" not vague CPU numbers.
- Avoid model names in first contact; call out "cost & latency" and "pilot timeline".
- When emailing CTO, include a single technical appendix PDF; keep main email conversational.

Slack reminders / internal comms (quick):
- #outbound-funnel: log sequence template + results
- #se-playbooks: upload one-pager + pilot runbook

Open questions to resolve before pilot pitch:
- exact qps and average seq length for their search calls
- whether they currently host any model weights (self-host) or consume a hosted LLM provider (this changes migration ask)

End note: keep this informal. This is experimental (A/B multiple subject lines, SDR+SE parallel outreach). If we get positive response — prioritize SE time in week 0 and ask for realistic dataset within 48 hours.

-- Jordan
